findings.claim: In SpanFlusher.join(), when the deadline expires the `break` exits the per-process loop before terminate() runs for the current and remaining flusher processes, leaving them running after join returns during shutdown/rebalance.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:337-347, once the deadline has passed, the `break` at line 341 leaves the loop before line 347 calls `process.terminate()`. The current process and every later one in `self.processes` are never terminated and can still be running when join returns (the stopped flag is set, so they should exit eventually).

findings.claim: The isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard before process.kill() in the restart path (_ensure_processes_alive) is always False for spawn-context SpawnProcess objects, so hung or unhealthy processes are never killed before replacements start. The pre-PR code called kill() unconditionally.

verifier.reason: In flusher.py (patch line 303), process.kill() only runs if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is true. On POSIX, CPython defines `SpawnProcess` as a subclass of `process.BaseProcess`, not of `multiprocessing.context.Process`, so this check is always false for the processes created by `mp_context.Process` (line 163). As a result, a hung process is left running while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement, whereas the old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally.

findings.claim: In join(), terminate() sits behind the same isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check, which is always False for SpawnProcess, so flusher processes are never terminated on shutdown or rebalance.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:346-347, join() only calls terminate() when isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is true. The processes come from get_context("spawn").Process, a SpawnProcess. In CPython both SpawnProcess and multiprocessing.Process subclass BaseProcess, but neither subclasses the other, so the check is always False and terminate() never runs; the same check was already there before the patch (old self.process check, patch lines 375-376).

findings.claim: _create_process_for_shard (lines 127-132) has no callers in src/ or tests/ and only delegates to _create_process_for_shards, so it is dead code.

verifier.reason: Searching the whole repo finds `_create_process_for_shard` only at its definition (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:127). Nothing calls it: `_create_processes` and `_ensure_processes_alive` both call `_create_process_for_shards` directly. The method only loops over the shard map and hands off to `_create_process_for_shards`, so it is dead code.

findings.claim: Having both _create_process_for_shard and _create_process_for_shards, with near-identical names, is confusing.

verifier.reason: The patch adds both methods: `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` at src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:86 and `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` at flusher.py:127. They differ by a single 's' but do different jobs, since the second looks up which process owns the shard and restarts that process. Nothing in the repository calls `_create_process_for_shard`, so the confusing name is also dead code.

findings.claim: In test_basic in test_consumer.py, the added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op earlier in the test, so it does not give the flusher time to process.

verifier.reason: test_consumer.py:396 patches the attribute on the `time` module with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`. The `time.sleep(0.1)` added at test_consumer.py:403 looks `sleep` up on that same module when it runs, so it calls the no-op lambda and waits for nothing.

findings.claim: test_flusher_processes_limit asserts only internal attributes and does not check that segments from all shards are flushed across multiple processes. No test covers the restart/kill path.

verifier.reason: In test_consumer.py (patch lines 444-451), test_flusher_processes_limit only checks `len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes` and the total shard count in `process_to_shards_map`. It never sends spans or checks that segments from every shard get flushed. A grep of tests/sentry/spans for `_ensure_processes_alive`, `process_restarts`, `kill`, `is_alive`, `flusher_unhealthy` and `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` finds nothing, so the per-process restart path in flusher.py (patch lines 251-308) has no test.

findings.claim: The CLI default for --flusher-processes is 1 (one process for all shards), while SpanFlusher and ProcessSpansStrategyFactory default max_processes to None (one per shard). This forces a single process, and tests exercise only the per-shard path.

verifier.reason: The defaults differ as described: --flusher-processes defaults to 1 (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:35-38 of the patch), while ProcessSpansStrategyFactory and SpanFlusher default to None, meaning one process per shard (flusher.py:98,103). But the CLI default is deliberate, since its help text says 'Defaults to 1', and the test claim is wrong: test_flusher_processes_limit (test_consumer.py:415-453) runs with flusher_processes=2 and 4 shards, so the shared-process path is tested.

findings.claim: The docstring 'Creates one process per shard' does not match the default deployment, where the CLI default of 1 runs all shards in one process. The comments at lines 178 and 235 also do not match the code.

verifier.reason: The CLI default is `--flusher-processes=1` (consumers/__init__.py), and flusher.py computes `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))`, so by default every shard runs in one process, not 'one process per shard'. The comment at flusher.py:235 says 'any shard' is checked, but the code checks a single per-process `process_healthy_since` value; the comment at :178 likewise suggests per-shard updates when there is only one value per process.

findings.claim: max_processes is normalised twice, self.max_processes is kept only for the test, and _create_processes is a 2-line wrapper with one caller.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py, max_processes is normalised at line 51 (`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`) and clamped again at line 60 (`min(self.max_processes, len(...))`). Apart from that constructor line, `self.max_processes` is read only by test_consumer.py:116, and `_create_processes` (lines 81-84) is a 2-line loop whose only caller is line 79.

findings.claim: --flusher-processes is a plain int with no lower bound: 0 silently means one process per shard, and a negative value gives a negative num_processes and an empty process_to_shards_map, causing a KeyError during shard distribution.

verifier.reason: The new click.Option at src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:433-438 is a plain `type=int` with no lower bound. In flusher.py (patch lines 103, 118-124), `max_processes or len(...)` turns 0 into one process per shard. A negative value gives `num_processes = min(-1, n) = -1`, so `range(-1)` builds an empty map and `process_to_shards_map[i % -1]` (key 0) raises KeyError.

findings.claim: submit() loops over one SpansBuffer per child process, calling get_memory_info() and record_stored_segments() N times against the same Redis cluster on the consumer main thread.

verifier.reason: In flusher.py, submit() loops over self.buffers.values(), which holds one SpansBuffer per process (patch lines 320-321 and 346-347). It calls record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() on each one, and every buffer uses the same cluster through get_redis_client() (buffer.py:117-118, 162-163). So the main thread runs iter_cluster_memory_usage (buffer.py:375-376) N times over the same nodes and opens N separate ZCARD pipelines.

findings.claim: The spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce timer (line 199) uses tag key 'shards', while the other metrics in the same flush loop (lines 185, 195, 244) use 'shard'.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:199 the wait_produce timer is tagged `{"shards": shard_tag}`, while the produce timer and counters at lines 185, 195 and 244 use the key "shard". Before this patch the wait_produce timer had no tags at all.

findings.claim: The 'shard' tag value at lines 185 and 195 is a comma-joined list of a process's shards, which changes on rebalance and has high cardinality. Line 244 tags a single int under the same key, and existing buffer metrics use 'shard_i'.

verifier.reason: At flusher.py:185 and :195 the `shard` tag is `shard_tag`, built as `",".join(map(str, shards))` from the process's assigned shards, and those shards come from the partition assignment that changes on rebalance. flusher.py:244 tags a single int under the same `shard` key, and the existing buffer metrics at buffer.py:372 and :447 use `shard_i`.

findings.claim: Several new comments (lines 59, 82, 92, 241, 336) restate the code.

verifier.reason: The comments are new in this patch and only repeat what the next line does: flusher.py:82 'Create processes based on shard mapping' above a loop calling _create_process_for_shards, :92 'Create a buffer for these specific shards' above SpansBuffer(shards), :241 'Report unhealthy for all shards…' above a per-shard metrics.incr loop, and :336 'Wait for all processes to finish' above the join loop. :59 is a loose paraphrase of the shard-to-process assignment.

findings.claim: The `if not process: continue` guard in _ensure_processes_alive can never be true, because self.processes only holds started Process or Thread objects, which are always truthy.

verifier.reason: self.processes is only ever written at src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:124, which stores a Process or Thread right after it is started. Neither SpawnProcess nor threading.Thread defines __bool__ or __len__, so these objects are always truthy and the `if not process: continue` guard at flusher.py:221-223 can never run.

findings.claim: The hasattr/isinstance anti-pattern guidance added to CLAUDE.md (lines 448-458) is unrelated to the span-flusher change.

verifier.reason: The new CLAUDE.md guidance (CLAUDE.md:448-458) says to narrow a union type with isinstance() instead of hasattr(), and the patch does exactly that in the flusher. At flusher.py:303 (patch line 303), it narrows the `SpawnProcess | threading.Thread` union from `self.processes` (patch line 126) with `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` before calling `kill()`, so the guidance matches a pattern the flusher change uses.

findings.claim: Each process's SpansBuffer computes ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)) over only its own shard subset, so spans.buffer.max-flush-segments becomes a per-process budget. Total flush per cycle and the backpressure threshold therefore scale with process count.

verifier.reason: flusher.py:152 now builds `SpansBuffer(shards)` for each process's subset of shards. buffer.py:382-384 then divides `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` by that subset size instead of the full shard count, so every process flushes up to the whole budget each cycle and the total grows with the number of processes. The limit check at buffer.py:411 uses the same `max_segments_per_shard`, so the backpressure threshold scales with process count too.
